Team — I reviewed Julia's sample. High-level notes and asks for validation: 

1) Validation objectives (what must pass before we unlock cutover window):
   - Sustained p95 latency under 250ms for human traffic profile at committed capacity
   - KV cache hit rate >= 65% for long-chat workflows during staging run
   - No >5% error-rate for model calls across the 24h window

2) Tests we will run:
   - Stitch their 7d trace into staging and run 2x real-time replay, plus one full-batch replay for the 02:00 UTC job.
   - Run a long seq stress (3.6k tokens) workload to validate memory/quantization tails.

3) Deliverables from SRE and Solutions: capacity sheet, KV/cache estimator, and a short runbook describing rollback conditions.

Neha — can you confirm we have the GPU mix available Jun 16–18 in East US region? Karthik — please draft a canary plan (warmup, traffic ramp schedule, success metrics) so we can send to the customer Friday.

I'll assemble a mutual action plan (MAP) doc once we have the canary timeline.

Rachel Kim
Sales Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference

- GPU mix: we can guarantee 8x A100-80GB-equivalent capacity during staging; for production cutover we'll need a 48–72 hour commit for additional burst GPUs if we need to absorb marketing spikes.
- KV/cache: preliminary model of their trace yields an estimated cache footprint of ~120GB (working set) with a projected hit-rate of 58% on default TTLs. See attached estimates with more scenarios.

I'll prepare a short checklist and the capacity spreadsheet (attached) with conservative and optimistic rows. If we want p95 latency headroom, we should provision an additional 20% burst capacity or tune batching thresholds.

Subject: RE: Novalyft onboarding: sizing sanity gates & cutover readiness

Suggested canary plan (summary):

1) Warmup (Day -1): deploy model variant to staging and run a 4-hour warm cache replay at 20% of production RPS. Check KV priming and cache hit stabilization.
2) Canary day (Day 0): route 10% of real traffic for 2 hours -> 30% for 3 hours -> 60% for 4 hours assuming no regressions. Each step requires green metrics (latency, error rate, tail memory).
3) Roll-forward criteria: success across 6 continuous hours with p95 < 250ms and no error-rate spike >1.5x baseline.
4) Rollback triggers: persistent p99 > 1.5s for >10 minutes, memory OOMs, or GPU saturation >92% for >15 minutes.

Operational asks for procurement/legal: we still need the signed MSA (mutual redlines completed) and capacity commitment sheet to finalize reserved capacity for cutover day. Ben — can you chase?

Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
